**Issue #2725 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #2725: Patch: ten new card versions (alt art, sketch, pixel, immersive and more) and a deeper rarity ladder, after Pokémon TCG Pocket; full arts rarer
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

## What it does

The owner's reference is Pokémon TCG Pocket's art rarities: https://www.pokemon-zone.com/articles/arts-rarities-in-tcg-pocket/. The page couldn't be fetched from the session that wrote this issue, so here is the ladder as generally known; check the page if you can reach it:

| Pocket tier | What it is |
|---|---|
| ◇ to ◇◇◇◇ | The regular prints; ◇◇◇◇ is the "ex" cards |
| ☆ Art Rare | A **new illustration**: the subject in a scene that runs behind the text, the text kept |
| ☆☆ Super Rare / Special Art Rare | **Full art**, textured, often a whole new scene |
| ☆☆☆ Immersive Rare | An animated scene the player can step into |
| 👑 Crown Rare | The card in gold (**not for JackiOh**: gold is Radiant's; see below) |
| ✦ / ✦✦ Shiny | Shiny variants |

The point is that the high tiers are a **different picture or treatment** of the card, not just the same picture made bigger.

After #2715 a card can wear four **versions**: Full art, Animated, Full art + animated, and Signature (full art + animated + signed). The owner wants **ten more**: more full arts, alt arts, anything, as long as **Radiant stays easy to tell apart**. Each version can also be **augmented by the other pulls** (§3). **Not every card needs every version.**

### 1. Ten new versions

Every card's art is procedural (`apps/web/src/cards/art/`: `procedural.ts`, `svg.ts`, `motifs.ts`, `themes.ts`, and the Stinkyscape and Training Grounds painters), so a version can be drawn for any card, as a pure function of the card's id, name, tags and type, base and Radiant faces both.

| # | Version | What it looks like | Proposed rarity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Alt art** | A new picture in the normal frame: the same subject in a new scene, pose or palette, the text kept (Pocket's Art Rare) | Rare |
| 2 | **Sketch** | The art as an artist's pencil-and-ink sketch on paper: line work, hatching, paper grain; the frame as a pencilled outline | Rare |
| 3 | **Extended art** | The card's own art bleeds past its window, behind a translucent rules box and frame (a borderless print) | Epic |
| 4 | **Pixel** | The art as 8-bit pixel art in a retro frame, with a pixel face for the name | Epic |
| 5 | **Comic** | Pop art: halftone dots, heavy ink outlines, flat bright colour, the name in a burst | Epic |
| 6 | **Set showcase** | The whole card restyled in its set's own look (frame, art treatment and type): Core's orbs, Classic's temple stone, Meditative's ink wash, Stinkyscape's deep space, Training Grounds' wood and rope | Legendary |
| 7 | **Alt full art** | Version 1's new picture across the whole face, as a full art (Pocket's Special Art Rare) | Legendary |
| 8 | **Out of frame** | The subject breaks out of its window and over the frame and edge, as if stepping out of the card | Legendary |
| 9 | **Immersive** | A layered scene with parallax depth that shifts with the pointer or the device's tilt and breathes slowly; still under reduced motion (Pocket's Immersive) | Mythic |
| 10 | **Prismatic** | Mirror-chrome, rainbow-edged and iridescent, the top chase. It replaces Pocket's gold Crown, because gold is Radiant's | Mythic, or the new top tier (§2) |

The builder may swap one for a better idea, keeping ten, all distinct from each other and from the existing four, and from what a foil, finish or border already does.

**Which cards get which versions: not all of them.** Each card is offered a subset, the versions that suit it. Pocket gives its special arts to some cards, not all. The plan picks the rule and records it as data, beside the registry: per card, per set, per rarity or per type, or a seeded pick. For example:

- every collectible card gets Alt art and one more;
- the rarer versions go to fewer cards, chosen where the style suits the card (Out of frame on Units with a strong subject, Set showcase on the sets' signature cards);
- Prismatic and Immersive go to a few marquee cards per set.

Each version should still reach a fair spread of cards across every shipped set. A version a card isn't offered is never dropped for it, sold for it, or shown as locked on it.

### 2. The ladder, and full arts rarer

The owner wants full art **rarer** overall. A proposal for every version's rarity (the plan finalises it):

| Cosmetic rarity | Versions |
|---|---|
| Rare | Alt art, Sketch |
| Epic | Animated (#2715), Extended art, Pixel, Comic |
| Legendary | **Full art (moved up from Epic)**, Set showcase, Alt full art, Out of frame |
| Mythic | **Full art + animated (moved up from Legendary)**, Immersive |
| New top tier above Mythic, if added | **Signature (moved up from Mythic)**, Prismatic |

- **If the plan adds the tier above Mythic,** it extends the cosmetics' rarity scale in one change: `CosmeticRarity` (`crates/server/src/cosmetics.rs`), `public.cosmetics.rarity`'s check (migration 0045), `COSMETIC_TIER_WEIGHTS`, pity, the token cycle and the Chase Shard (§14.3 to §14.6, with each odds table on `/purchases`), plus the client's rarity styling. If it stays within Common to Mythic, it says why.
- **More versions per tier already makes each one rarer.** With more versions sharing a tier, any one version is rarer to roll.
- **Full art becomes general:** offered on many more cards than the 21, under the same "suits the card" rule. The 21 hand-picked cards keep their current full arts.

### 3. Versions are augmented by the other pulls

A card wears **one version** (its base look: normal, a full art, or one of the ten), and the other things a player pulls **layer on top** of it:

- **Animated** (#2715's motion: the art's own elements moving), on any version whose art can move;
- **Signature** (the signed name), on any version;
- the card's **foil**, **finish** and **border** (§14.2), as they do on a normal face (#2720 makes the finishes work on full-bleed faces).

So a player can wear, say, Sketch + Animated + a foil, or Alt full art + Signature + a border. Animated and Signature become **augments**, owned per card like a foil, that apply to whichever version the card wears. #2715's combined cosmetics (Full art + animated, and Signature) stay owned as they are, and the plan maps them onto the new model so that nobody loses anything. For example, owning Full art + animated on a card counts as owning Full art and the Animated augment on that card.

**Not every combination has to look distinct,** and none may break: no layer hidden, nothing unreadable, no Radiant mark lost. The builder may rule out a pairing that can't work (say, Signature on Pixel) and give the reason in the ruling. The picker then doesn't offer it.

### 4. How a version is stored and picked

- **One registry entry per version and per augment, owned card by card**, the way a foil, finish or border is (`is_per_card` in `cosmetics.rs`; `card_cosmetics` rows), rather than one entry per version per card. The latter would be roughly 14 × 634 ≈ 9,000 entries.
- **The availability rule from §1** says which cards may own and wear each one.
- **The 21 hand-picked full arts** keep their per-card ids from R2655000, so nobody's ownership changes.
- **A card's pick:** one version, plus its augments, plus foil, finish and border. Today's `fullArt` pick (and migration 0072's `full_art_id` check) widens, or a new `version` pick with `augments` replaces it. Either way the server holds every part of the pick to ownership on that card and to the availability rule (R1834001), freezes it in a match's loadout, and shows it to the opponent, watchers and replays (R1834002, R1834004).

### 5. Radiant stays easy to tell apart

A Radiant face is a gold-foil frame whatever the rarity (`.cf[data-radiant-face="true"]`, `apps/web/src/cards/cards.css`), R277's gold marks on what it prints that the base doesn't, gold raised stats, its art's gold rays or tint, and Radiant foil. It is a different face with different text and stats, so a player must never mistake one.

- **No version or augment uses Radiant's gold** on its frame, edge, text marks or stats, and none tints a base face's art gold. Prismatic is chrome, never gold.
- **Every version keeps Radiant's marks on a Radiant face,** with any augments on: the gold-foil frame (a gold rim on full-bleed versions such as Extended art, Alt full art, Out of frame and Immersive), R277's marks wherever text shows, the gold stats, and the Radiant paint on its picture (the rays or the tint). The base and Radiant faces of one version differ just as the normal card's do.
- **Every version keeps the card readable:** the cost gem, the type's panel colour (a Radiant Trap still reads red), the crest, the stats, the name (except in hand, #2723) and the rules text at the box's contrast floor.

### Constraints

- **No one loses anything.** An account keeps every cosmetic it owns by id. A rarity change moves only future drops and token prices, and is written down in §14.12's going-live notes.
- **Every new version and augment starts unowned,** granted to no account (§14.12, as R1833000 and R2655000). `POST /api/dev/fill` grants each one on every card that is offered it.
- **The Collection shows each card's versions:** normal, then the ones the card is offered (owned or locked), with rarities and a preview, and the augments to toggle on top.
- **Motion:** the animated looks (Animated on any version, Immersive) take motion slots (`COSMETIC_FOIL_ANIMATED_MAX`) so a grid of cards stays smooth. They are still under reduced motion and with Animated foil off.
- **Presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7):** no rule reads a version, and nothing enters `PlayerView`'s rules, an action, the log or a replay hash.

This needs a ruling note in this issue's block, amends R1313000, R1333000 and R2655000, and updates SPEC §14.2 to §14.6 and §14.12. It changes how cards look, so it takes a pending fragment; whether the owner names it a system release (`SYSTEM_RELEASES`) is for the plan to state.

**Split it.** This is too big for one pull request, so plan it as a tree (`bot:tree`):
1. The version slot, the augments, the availability rule, the registry entries, the ladder and rarity change, the server, the migration and the Collection.
2. Then the ten versions in a few parts of two or three each, the art first and the animated ones last.

If the planner finds an owner decision it cannot make, it should stop with `human_required` and list the questions, rather than guess.

## Acceptance

- The registry holds the ten new versions and the augments with their rarities, its check passes, and `public.cosmetics` is seeded with them. If a tier above Mythic is added, the migration, weights, pity and odds tables all take it, and the server's economy tests and `sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh` pass.
- The availability rule is data. A test holds every version to at least a named number of cards spread across every shipped set, and every offered (card, version) pair to drawing without error, base and Radiant, and differing from the card's normal face.
- A version a card isn't offered is never rolled, sold or picked for it: the server refuses it with a 400 and writes nothing, and the Collection doesn't list it.
- Animated and Signature layer on every version they are offered on, and a foil, finish and border on every version. Each ruled-out pairing is listed in the ruling and refused by the picker and the server. #2715's combined cosmetics still show exactly as before for an account that owns them.
- **Radiant:** for each version, with and without its augments, a Radiant face shows Radiant's marks (gold frame or rim, R277 marks, gold stats, Radiant art paint) and a base face shows none. A test holds every version's and augment's palette clear of the Radiant golds (`--radiant` and the gold-foil frame's stops).
- Full art drops at its new, rarer tier, on the cards the rule offers it to. An account that owned a full art still owns it, and no account gains any new cosmetic.
- A pick (version and augments) is accepted only where each part is owned and offered on that card (400 otherwise, nothing written), and is frozen and shown to the other seat. Each has a test.
- A component (pixel) spec shows each version on one Unit and one Spell, base and Radiant, with an augment stack (Animated + Signature + a foil) on two of them.
- The animated looks take motion slots and hold still under reduced motion.
- The ruling note and the amended rulings pass `cargo jackioh spec check`, and `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` passes.

## Blocked by, part of

Blocked by #2715, which adds the Animated Epic and real animation; this issue builds the ladder and the augments on top of it.
```
